subject: Setting bootstrap in sem() and/or parameterEstimates()

messages.author: 873e62093c762b35
messages.subject: Setting bootstrap in sem() and/or parameterEstimates()
parts:
1. When setting bootstrap, I noticed that the results differ when:
  • The bootstrap is set early on when fitting the model
    • fit=sem(model, data, se="bootstrap", bootstrap=5000)
    • and then, running parameterEstimates(fit, level=0.95, boot.ci.type="bca.simple")
  • OR, the bootstrap is set when estimating the parameter, where
    • fit=sem(model, data)
    • parameterEstimates(fit, level=0.95, boot.ci.type="bca.simple")
Are both of these approaches correct?

2. Another question I had was for boot.ci.type, is there a way to get standard errors for bootstrapping based on percentile method (rather than bootstrapping and accelerated)?

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Setting bootstrap in sem() and/or parameterEstimates()
parts: 1. When setting bootstrap, I noticed that the results differ when:
• The bootstrap is set early on when fitting the model

• fit=sem(model, data, se="bootstrap", bootstrap=5000)
    • and then, running parameterEstimates(fit, level=0.95, boot.ci.type="bca.simple")
• In this case you are looking at standard error and CI based on the 5000 bootstrap you asked
• OR, the bootstrap is set when estimating the parameter, where

• fit=sem(model, data)
    • parameterEstimates(fit, level=0.95, boot.ci.type="bca.simple")
• In this case you are seeing results based on the Wlad tests, no boostrap has be asked. You need to include the arguments se="bootstrap", bootstrap=5000in the sem funtion to get bootstrap results
Are both of these approaches correct?
Only the first is actually doing boostrap
2. Another question I had was for boot.ci.type, is there a way to get standard errors for bootstrapping based on percentile method (rather than bootstrapping and accelerated)?
Specified boot.ci.type = "perc" in the parameterestimates function, this will give you results based on the percentile boostrap

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Setting bootstrap in sem() and/or parameterEstimates()
parts:
Julian

From the help page f parameterestimates: The "bca.simple" option produces intervals using the adjusted bootstrap percentile (BCa) method, but with no correction for acceleration (only for bias).
It seems this is what you are looking for

For other types you can look at bootstrapLavaan
